title: IOPsych — Mobbin design references
scope: Public Mobbin Explore previews, visually inspected. These are reference captures, not a claim about each product's latest release, accessibility, or effectiveness.
recommendation: Attio for the workspace and role list; Front for contextual detail pages; Midday for visual restraint; Origin and stoic. for the candidate experience.

references.observed: A quiet sidebar, compact toolbar, aligned column headers, and thinly divided record rows.
references.adapt: Use a 224px sidebar and a readable role table with title, department, location, stored role status, and created date. Keep a single Create role action. Use search and filters only when implemented against actual records.
references.leave_out: CRM integrations, contact-strength fields, excessive tag colors, bulk-selection controls without supported actions, and invented profile-status counts. Role status and profile approval are different facts.

references.observed: Navigation, a selected-record list, and the main reading pane remain visible together. Actions sit next to the selected object's title.
references.adapt: Keep role identity and version context near the evidence being reviewed. Put version history in a narrow contextual column and the six constructs in the main pane. Position approval beside the profile state and invitations beside the role identity.
references.leave_out: Chat composers, assignment controls, extra side rails, and new review-state or note-taking workflows without agreed product behavior. Collapse context below the title on mobile.

references.observed: White surfaces, black typography, hairline dividers, restrained chart color, and generous space around the main content.
references.adapt: Use ink text on white, a pale neutral navigation surface, and one muted violet accent for selection and focus. Let headings, spacing, and dividers organize the page. Use tabular numbers only for dates or aligned factual quantities.
references.leave_out: Revenue charts, oversized score numbers, unexplained trend deltas, icon-only navigation, and dashboard metrics that the application cannot substantiate.

references.observed: A focused headline, large text-based answer rows, a visibly selected option, and one obvious Next action.
references.adapt: Use a narrow reading column and comfortably sized text-based controls. Keep each forced-choice block's statements together; distinguish Most like me and Least like me with text, checked controls, and shape. Preserve answer review and the existing submission boundary.
references.leave_out: Finance copy, illustrated answer cues, a huge headline on every question, and single-select interest behavior substituted for the existing forced-choice rules. Do not add a skip option to required answers.

references.observed: A slim segmented progress indicator and strong filled-versus-outline selection states on a quiet canvas.
references.adapt: Use six progress segments with an explicit Block n of 6 label. Make checked states legible without color and retain visible keyboard focus. Use a single named Continue action with Back available when the existing flow supports it.
references.leave_out: Icon-only choices, an unlabeled floating arrow, unsupported multi-selection, wellbeing content, or illustrations that suggest which assessment answer is preferable.

references.observed: A pale persistent sidebar separates navigation from a bright content canvas, with compact labeled navigation entries.
references.adapt: Keep Roles, Privacy, and authorized Accounts together in a labeled sidebar. Put the signed-in identity and sign-out action at the bottom on desktop. Show the organization name where available; put the technical identifier in a details disclosure.
references.leave_out: The AI prompt hero, arbitrary nested pages, recent-document cards, calendars, and a dashboard homepage with no demonstrated need.

references.observed: Breadcrumbs and one object title establish context; tabs and labeled sections organize related details.
references.use_for: Role detail structure and report provenance
references.adapt: Keep role title, version, and state above the content. Group profile evidence, source description, invitations, and reports under clear headings or real navigation links. Keep algorithm and provenance details in an explicit expandable section for reviewers.
references.leave_out: Database terminology, deeply nested navigation, nonfunctional tabs, and hiding essential assessment limitations inside technical details.

references.observed: A people database uses labeled columns, compact avatars, quiet empty values, and a toolbar aligned with the data.
references.adapt: Use a plain table with actual account name, role, and access state. Keep privacy searches bounded to the existing exact-reference workflow. Place consequence text and confirmation beside each sensitive action.
references.leave_out: Social handles, phone numbers, follower counts, broad person search, and new candidate metadata. The reference is table organization, not a proposal to collect these fields.

references.observed: History entries align time, status, and contextual details under stable column headers.
references.use_for: Audit history and invitation delivery evidence
references.adapt: Make actor, action, timestamp, and stored outcome easy to scan. Distinguish queued, sent, uncertain, revoked, and used states in words using the existing API meanings. Expose a selected event's details progressively.
references.leave_out: Query text, unrelated operational fields, unbounded audit browsing, and treating provider acceptance as candidate completion.

references.observed: A visible Step 4 of 6 label, wide text choices, and a consistent bottom Continue action.
references.adapt: Keep current progress and the next action in predictable positions. Support wrapping answer text, comfortable touch targets, and back navigation. Keep the block counter independent of consent and completion stages.
references.leave_out: Orange gradients, pill-shaped choices when they hurt multiline readability, finance advice, and the source screen's multi-select semantics.

references.observed: A charcoal canvas, violet primary action, and compact status rows create a more technical visual mood.
references.adapt: Use it to compare mood and contrast with the proposed light workspace. Its compact status rows are relevant even if the product remains light.
references.leave_out: Defaulting every screen to dark mode, alarm-driven language, incident tooling, and an onboarding checklist that displaces the user's actual work.

design_spec.typography: Use one sans-serif family. Body 14–16px; primary page heading 26–30px; section heading 16–18px; supporting labels 12–13px. Most text stays regular or medium weight. Candidate statements remain at least 16px.
design_spec.geometry: 224px desktop navigation; 48–56px role rows; 32px desktop content gutters; 16–20px mobile gutters; 6–10px control corners; 44px minimum touch targets. Avoid a border and shadow around every section.
design_spec.responsive: At 900px, replace the desktop sidebar with compact labeled navigation. At 600px, render list records as stacked labeled rows and place context above the main reading pane. Keep candidate content within a 640px reading column.
design_spec.motion: Use 120–160ms state feedback only; honor reduced motion. No ambient animation or decorative progress.

first_pass: Build the shared shell and the roles list together, with real empty, loading, error, populated, and keyboard states.
Redesign one role detail page: stable identity/actions, compact maintenance, version context, and six evidence sections.
Carry the same hierarchy to reports while keeping limitations and supporting evidence clearly visible.
Design the candidate surface separately using Origin's readable choices and stoic.'s progress clarity, preserving consent and forced-choice behavior.
Apply the table system to invitation status, accounts, and exact-reference privacy workflows. Verify responsive layout and native dialogs.
rights_note: Public Mobbin previews retained with original attribution for private design research. These are not application assets or code licenses. Do not ship the screenshots, logos, or proprietary interface assets in the product.
